question_groups.title: Safety objectives and technical documentation (Annex I, Annex III)

questions.label: What is the highest AC voltage rating of the product's electrical inputs and outputs?
questions.guidance: Use the rated supply or output voltage marked on the product (RMS), not voltages that only occur inside it. Enter 0 if the product has no AC input or output. A mains-powered appliance is typically rated 230 V; equipment powered only by an external adapter is rated at the adapter's output, and the adapter is a product of its own.

questions.label: What is the highest DC voltage rating of the product's electrical inputs and outputs?
questions.guidance: Use the rated DC supply or output voltage, e.g. of a battery pack, a DC input or a charger output. Enter 0 if the product has no DC input or output.

questions.label: Is this a basic component whose safety depends mainly on how it is built into other equipment?
questions.guidance: Examples are resistors, capacitors, transistors and bare circuit boards. Components that are electrical equipment in their own right (switches, lamp holders, cable sets, power supplies, motors) are not basic components and stay in scope.

questions.label: Does the product belong to one of the categories excluded from the Low Voltage Directive?
questions.guidance: Excluded: equipment for explosive atmospheres; electrical parts of goods and passenger lifts; electricity meters; plugs and socket outlets for domestic use; electric fence controllers; specialised equipment for ships, aircraft or railways that meets safety provisions of international bodies in which the Member States take part; custom-built evaluation kits for professionals, used only at research and development facilities. Medical devices are asked separately. Most excluded products fall under other EU or national rules instead.

questions.label: How do you show that the product meets the safety objectives?
questions.guidance: Harmonised standards cited in the Official Journal give a presumption of conformity for the risks they cover. Where none exists, IEC standards published under the directive's procedure, and then national standards of the Member State of manufacture, can give it. Anything not covered needs your own solutions, described in the technical documentation.

exclude.ref: Annex II (equipment for radiology and medical purposes)

requirements.label: Make available only equipment built to good engineering practice in safety matters that does not endanger persons, domestic animals or property when properly installed, maintained and used
Mark the essential characteristics, make the equipment and its parts safe to assemble and connect, and design it against the hazards in Annex I points 2 and 3
Protect persons and domestic animals against injury from direct or indirect contact
Prevent dangerous temperatures, arcs or radiation
Protect persons, domestic animals and property against non-electrical dangers known from experience
Provide insulation suitable for foreseeable conditions
Meet the expected mechanical requirements so persons, domestic animals and property are not endangered
Resist non-mechanical influences in the expected environmental conditions
Do not endanger persons, domestic animals or property in foreseeable overload conditions
Draw up the technical documentation, including the risk analysis, and carry out internal production control
Draw up the EU declaration of conformity and keep it up to date
Affix the CE marking
Keep the technical documentation and the declaration of conformity for 10 years after the equipment is placed on the market
Keep series production in conformity; where the risks call for it, sample-test, investigate complaints and keep a register of complaints, non-conforming equipment and recalls
Mark a type, batch or serial number or other identification
Indicate the manufacturer's name, registered trade name or trademark and postal address
Supply instructions and safety information in a language easily understood by users
Take corrective action for non-conforming equipment and inform the authorities of risks
Give the authorities information and documentation on request and cooperate on eliminating risks
Keep the declaration of conformity and technical documentation available for 10 years, provide them on request, and cooperate with the authorities under the mandate
Place only compliant equipment on the market
Check that the manufacturer has carried out the conformity assessment, drawn up the technical documentation, affixed the CE marking, supplied the documents and identified the equipment
Indicate the importer's name, registered trade name or trademark and postal address
Ensure instructions and safety information accompany the equipment in a language easily understood by users
Ensure storage and transport conditions do not jeopardise conformity
Where the risks call for it, sample-test, investigate complaints and keep a register
Take corrective action for non-conforming equipment and inform the authorities of risks
Keep a copy of the declaration of conformity for 10 years and ensure the technical documentation can be made available
Give the authorities information and documentation on request and cooperate on eliminating risks
Act with due care in relation to the requirements of the directive
Check the CE marking, the documents, the instructions and safety information, and the manufacturer's and importer's identification
Ensure storage and transport conditions do not jeopardise conformity
Make sure corrective action is taken for non-conforming equipment and inform the authorities of risks
Give the authorities information and documentation on request and cooperate on eliminating risks

finding_rules.message: Below the LVD voltage ranges. Consumer products are covered by the General Product Safety Regulation (EU) 2023/988 instead; radio equipment by RED, with no voltage limit.
Above the LVD voltage ranges: the directive does not apply. Check other legislation (for example the Machinery Regulation) and national rules.
Radio equipment: the LVD safety objectives apply through RED Art. 3(1)(a), with no voltage limit. Assess electrical safety under the RED package.

Radio hardware present but disabled (physically, or until a manufacturer update): the product is under LVD, not RED, while the radio stays disabled. Enabling it makes the product radio equipment and requires re-assessment under RED.
No presumption of conformity for the risks not covered by harmonised standards: the technical documentation must describe the solutions adopted for them and the risk analysis must cover them.

International or national standards give a presumption of conformity only where no harmonised standard covers the risk, and only for standards published under the directive's procedure. Check the current list.
Document a risk analysis and assessment; the technical documentation must include it.
Complete the technical documentation before placing the product on the market.
Mark the electrical ratings and other essential characteristics on the equipment, or in an accompanying document.
Draw up the EU declaration of conformity before placing the product on the market.
Affix the CE marking before placing the product on the market.
Mark a type, batch or serial number and the manufacturer's name and postal address on the units, or on the packaging or documents where that is not possible.
Supply instructions and safety information in a language easily understood by users in every Member State where the product is sold.
Check the CE marking, the instructions and safety information and the identification of the manufacturer and importer before supplying the product.
Placing the product under your own name or modifying it makes you the manufacturer: the manufacturer's obligations apply to you.
Open-source steward is not a role under the LVD. Answer as manufacturer, importer, distributor or authorised representative for this product.
All units were placed on the market before 20 April 2016: they may still be made available if they conform to the previous directive, 2006/95/EC.
